messages.author: 0992bf1088c4051b
messages.subject: Frequency histogram
parts:
How can i make the histogram in ggplot2 just with the frequency table
and not with all data?
I mean, if i have something like this

endurance (hours) lamps (number)
0 - 100 82
100 - 200 71
200 - 300 68
300 - 400 56
400 - 500 43
500 - 800 15

I was able just to do it in package agricolae with graph.freq()

Thanks in advance

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Frequency histogram
parts:
Hi Felipe,

Does something like this do what you want?

dat <- sample(0:800, 400, replace = TRUE)
dat <- as.data.frame(table(cut(dat, seq(0,800,100))))

ggplot(data = dat, aes(x = Var1, y = Freq)) + geom_histogram()


HTH,

Josh

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: Frequency histogram
parts:
Hi Felipe,
I think you want something like

dat <- read.table(textConnection('endurance lamps

"0 - 100"     82
"100 - 200"       71
"200 - 300"       68
"300 - 400"       56
"400 - 500"       43

"500 - 800"       15'), header=TRUE)
closeAllConnections()

library(ggplot2)

dat$endurance.n <- 1:dim(dat)[1]
ggplot(dat, aes(x=endurance.n)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(weight=lamps), binwidth=1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=dat$endurance.n, labels=dat$endurance)

Best,
Ista

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Frequency histogram
parts:
Hi:

Not that I endorse this type of histogram as a general rule, but perhaps this would be suitable:

dat2 <- dat    # copy original df as a backup
# Alter some values in the 500-800 category - idea is to copy it twice for three copies,
# divide the total frequency by 3 in these replicate categories and remove the
# text except for the middle one of the replicated categories
dat[7:8, ] <- dat[6, ]          # replicate last row twice
dat[6:8, 2] <- 5                 # divide frequency by 3 in each of these categories
dat[7:8, 3] <- c(7, 8)        # replace frequency.n
dat$endurance <- as.character(dat$endurance)   # change first var to character
dat[c(6, 8), 1] <- ""          # blank out text in edges of the three replicated categories
dat
  endurance lamps endurance.n
1   0 - 100    82           1
2 100 - 200    71           2
3 200 - 300    68           3
4 300 - 400    56           4
5 400 - 500    43           5
6               5           6
7 500 - 800     5           7
8               5           8
str(dat)
'data.frame':   8 obs. of  3 variables:
 $ endurance  : chr  "0 - 100" "100 - 200" "200 - 300" "300 - 400" ...
 $ lamps      : num  82 71 68 56 43 5 5 5
 $ endurance.n: num  1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8

# Subtract 0.5 from the breaks to center the labels

ggplot(dat, aes(x=endurance.n)) +
   geom_histogram(aes(weight=lamps), binwidth=1) +

scale_x_continuous(breaks=dat$endurance.n - 0.5, labels=dat$endurance)

Normally, you'd want a color aesthetic to demarcate the categories, but not
in this case because you're using three categories to represent one long one.
The frequencies are divided by three in each constructed subcategory
in order to maintain the correct area.

Dennis
